sentences.text:
Smt. Varsha Singh Thakur - Govt Advocate for the respon
Record of the trial Court has been received.
Heard on the question of admission.
Appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A. no. 99/2023 which is an application filed under section 389 of Cr.P.C on behalf of appellant Dharmendra for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

2/ The appellant has been convicted under section 363, 366 and 376(2)
(n) of IPC and sentenced to undergo three years R.I with fine of Rs. 2000/-; five years R.I with fine of Rs. 3000/- and ten years R.I with fine of Rs. 5000/- respectively with default stipulation.
3/ Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
The appellant is in jail since 13/06/2017 and has already suffered jail incarceration for more than six years..
The prosecutrix was consenting party and was major at the time of the incident.
Date of birth of the prosecutrix recorded in the scholar register is based upon the assumption and without any support of documentary evidence.
The prosecutrix has also solemnized marriage with other person.
There is material contradictions and omissions in the statement of the prosecution witnesses There is strong case in favour of the appellant.
Final disposal of the appeal will take considerable long time.
Under these circumstances, he prays that the application be allowed and the remaining jail sentence of the appellant be suspended till final disposal of the appeal.

4/ Learned GA for the respondent/State opposed the prayer for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence of the appellant by submitting that the appellant has been properly convicted and sentenced by the trial Court.

sentences.text:
1 5/ Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties as also from perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix (PW-3), it appears that she wanted to marry with the appellant, but she came to know that the appellant was already married with some other lady; as per the scholar register, the prosecutrix's date of birth is 11/08/1999; her mother Suganbai (PW-2) deposed that her age is 40 years and her marriage was solemnized about 30 years ago and after five years of marriage, she gave birth to a son Arun and after three years of birth of Arun, the prosecutrix was borne, but statement of Suganbai does not appear to be trustworthy, because she is an illiterate lady and she has no understanding about her own age and age of her children; final disposal of appeal is likely to take time, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence and grant bail to the appellant.
6/ Accordingly, IA No. 99/2023 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal and it is ordered that the appellant be released on bail upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 18/12/2023 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.
